transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. My mind feels foggy all the time—I can’t focus at work or even finish a simple puzzle like I used to. It has gotten to the point where I'm really worried about how it's affecting my daily life.
Is this the first time you have experienced these feelings of brain fog and difficulty focusing, or have you had similar episodes in the past?
Yes, this is the first time I've ever felt this way. I've never really had episodes like this in the past, at least nothing this severe.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, such as changes in your energy levels, sleep patterns, or any new medical conditions?

Yes, my body feels incredibly heavy and slow, like I'm trying to move through mud. I've also lost my appetite and noticed my work uniform is fitting looser, though I don't have any new medical conditions. My sleep has been relatively normal, but physically I just feel completely drained.
Do you find that you have lost interest or pleasure in the hobbies and activities you used to enjoy, or do you still feel motivated to do things despite the physical heaviness?

Yes, I've really lost interest in the things I used to love, like cooking with my wife or playing guitar with my kid. Now, I just sit on the couch staring at the TV because I don't have the motivation to do anything. My body also feels incredibly heavy and slow, like I'm moving through mud, which makes it even harder to get up and do anything.
On a scale of 1 to 10, how much would you say these symptoms are interfering with your ability to perform your daily tasks at work or at home?

I’d rate it an 8 or 9 out of 10 because it’s seriously impacting both my job and my home life. My supervisor has already pulled me aside twice for missing things on the security monitors, which is really concerning. At home, my marriage is under heavy strain because I'm just too checked out to engage with my wife and child.

Besides feeling heavy and slow, have you noticed any periods where you feel completely unable to react to your environment, or do you find that your thoughts have slowed down significantly to the point where it is difficult to hold a conversation?

I don't feel completely paralyzed, but my mind is incredibly sluggish, like it's full of cotton. I often zone out or get stuck on simple decisions like what to make for breakfast, and my wife says I'm so emotionally checked out that I struggle to follow conversations and just sit there silently.

Would you say that you are still able to experience any positive emotions or feel a temporary lift in your mood if something good happens, or do you feel a profound lack of reactivity to your surroundings most of the time?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I mostly just feel empty, checked out, and like I'm going through the motions every day. I can't really remember the last time something gave me a temporary lift in my mood.
If you were to receive some very good news or have something positive happen, do you feel that your mood would brighten, even if just for a short time?
I'm really not sure. It's hard to even imagine anything lifting this heavy, empty feeling right now, even if it was really good news.
Do you feel that you have lost all capacity for pleasure in your daily life, to the point where even the prospect of good news fails to make you feel any better?

Yes, I really feel like I’ve lost any ability to enjoy things. I don't look forward to cooking with my wife or playing guitar with my kid anymore, and I just end up staring at the TV. It feels like nothing, not even really good news, could penetrate or lift this heavy, empty feeling.

I have sufficient information to conclude the assessment.
